'''André Aptroot''' ([[Heemskerk]], 1961) is a Dutch [[mycologist]] and [[lichenologist]]. His primary research focus is on [[biodiversity]], particularly tropical lichens, encompassing [[systematics]], [[floristic]] surveys, and [[taxonomy (biology)|taxonomic]] reviews. A prolific researcher, he has published more than 500 scientific papers and described hundreds of new fungal and lichen species.

==Career==
In 1993 he did his [[PhD]] at the [[University of Utrecht]] under the supervision of [[:nl:Robbert Gradstein|Robbert Gradstein (nl)]]. His [[dissertation]] was titled "Systematic studies on pyrenocarpous lichens and related fungi".<ref name="Kärnefelt 1993"/>

He specializes in [[fungi]] and [[lichen]]s on which he has several hundreds of publications to his name. He has worked as [[curator]] at [[Centraalbureau voor Schimmelcultures]] (now Westerdijk Institute).<ref name="Kärnefelt 2008"/>

Aptroot is the founder of the ''Adviesbureau voor Bryologie en Lichenologie – Herbarium'' (Consultancy for Bryology and Lichenology), which is located in [[Soest, Netherlands|Soest]] where there is a [[herbarium]] with a collection of lichens mainly from the [[Netherlands]] and the [[tropics]]. This collection numbers into the tens of thousands of specimens, estimated to represent about 10,000 species.<ref name="Kärnefelt 2008"/> From 2008 he has been collection manager at [[:nl:Pinetum Blijdenstein|Pinetum Blijdenstein (nl)]] in [[Hilversum]]. He is a member of the [[International Association for Lichenology]]<ref>[http://www.lichenology.org/ International Association for Lichenology]</ref> and the [[American Bryological and Lichenological Society]].

He is a visiting professor at the [[Federal University of Mato Grosso do Sul]] in Campo Grande, Brazil, since February 2019. In 2020, Aptroot was listed among the 100,000 most influential scientists in the world according to research published by [[Stanford University]], which utilised citations from the [[Scopus]] database. The research highlighted scientists' impact throughout their careers and in the year 2019 specifically.<ref name="UFMS"/> Because of Aptroot's broad expertise in tropical lichens, his colleague [[Ingvar Kärnefelt]] has called him "a [[Johannes Müller Argoviensis|Müller Argoviensis]] of our time".<ref name="Kärnefelt 2008"/> Aptroot is the author or co-author of three of the thirty most highly cited publications published in the scientific journal ''[[The Lichenologist]]'' from 2000 to 2019.<ref name="Lücking 2021"/> He is also a prolific author (or co-author) of new fungal and lichen species, having [[species description|formally described]] 775 as of December 2017.<ref name="Lücking 2020"/> Starting with 2017 he acts as co-editor of the [[exsiccata]] series ''Lichenes Neotropici'', together with [[Klaus Kalb]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Lichenes Neotropici: IndExs ExsiccataID=2147199835 |website=IndExs – Index of Exsiccatae |publisher=Botanische Staatssammlung München |url=https://www.botanischestaatssammlung.de/DatabaseClients/IndExs/Exsiccatae_IndExs_Details.jsp?ExsiccataID=2147199835 |access-date=24 May 2024}}</ref>

==Eponymy==
[[File:Lecidea aptrootii (10.3897-mycokeys.38.26960) Figure 4.jpg|thumb|right|''[[Lecidea aptrootii]]'' is one of many species named after Aptroot.]]
Several [[taxon|taxa]] have [[eponym|been named]] to honour Aptroot. These include the genera ''[[Aptrootia]]'' {{small|Lücking & Sipman (2007)}} and ''[[Aptrootidea]]'' {{small|Xavier-Leite, M.Cáceres & Lücking (2023)}}<ref name="Xavier-Leite et al. 2023"/> and the following species: ''[[Mazosia aptrootii]]'' {{small|Sipman (1991)}};<ref name="Sipman 1991"/> ''[[Buellia aptrootii]]'' {{small|Sipman (1992)}};<ref name="Sipman & Aptroot 1992"/> ''[[Parmotrema aptrootii]]'' {{small|Aubel (1992)}};<ref name="Sipman & Aubel 1992"/> ''[[Byssoloma aptrootii]]'' {{small|Sérus. (1993)}};<ref name="Sérusiaux 1993"/> ''[[Porina aptrootii]]'' {{small|P.M.McCarthy (1993)}};<ref name="McCarthy 1993"/> ''[[Pertusaria aptrootii]]'' {{small|A.W.Archer & Elix (1998)}};<ref name="Archer & Elix 1998"/> ''[[Didymella aptrootii]]'' {{small|K.D.Hyde & S.W. Wong (1999)}};<ref name="Hyde & Wong 1999"/> ''[[Lecidella aptrootii]]'' {{small|Knoph & Garnitz (1999)}};<ref name="Knoph et al. 1999"/> ''[[Sclerophyton aptrootii]]'' {{small|Sparrius (2004)}};<ref name="Sparrius 2004"/> ''[[Alloconiothyrium aptrootii]]'' {{small|Verkley, Göker & Stielow (2014)}};<ref name="Verkley et al. 2014"/> ''[[Graphis aptrootiana]]'' {{small|Van den Broeck, Lücking & Ertz (2014)}};<ref name="Broeck et al. 2014"/> ''[[Ocellularia aptrootiana]]'' {{small|Weerakoon, Lücking & Lumbsch (2014)}};<ref name="Weerakoon et al. 2014"/> ''[[Sclerococcum aptrootii]]'' {{small|Diederich (2015)}};<ref name="Diederich 2015"/> ''[[Myxospora aptrootii]]'' {{small|L.Lombard & Crous (2016)}};<ref name="Lombard et al. 2016"/> ''[[Hazslinszkyomyces aptrootii]]'' {{small|Crous (2017)}};<ref name="Crous & Groenewald 2017"/> ''[[Gyalideopsis aptrootii]]'' {{small|Xavier-Leite, M.Cáceres & Lücking (2018)}};<ref name="Xavier-Leiteda et al. 2018"/> ''[[Lecidea aptrootii]]'' {{small|M.Khan, A.N.Khalid & Lumbsch (2018)}};<ref name="Khan et al. 2018"/> ''[[Pseudochapsa aptrootiana]]'' {{small|M.Cáceres, T.A.Pereira & Lücking (2018)}};<ref name="Pereira et al. 2018"/> ''[[Ionaspis aptrootii]]'' {{au|Poengs. & Lumbsch (2021)}};<ref name="Poengsungnoen et al. 2021"/> ''[[Carbacanthographis aptrootii]]'' {{small|Feuerstein & Lücking (2022)}};<ref name="Feuerstein et al. 2022"/> ''[[Tremella aptrootii]]'' {{small|Diederich & Common (2022)}};<ref name="Diederich et al. 2022"/> and ''[[Verrucaria aptrootii]]'' {{small|M.S.Iqbal & Khalid (2024)}}.<ref name="Iqbal & Khalid 2024"/>
